page.title: Best Power Station Under $1,000 (2026): Ranked by Measured Usable Watt-Hours per Dollar
page.desc: Five power stations under $1,000 ranked by usable watt-hours and continuous watts per dollar, using The Solar Lab's measured efficiency and idle draw for each.
page.answer: Short answer. The best portable power station under $1,000 at Black Friday 2026 prices is the Pecron F3000LFP: $899 for 3,072 Wh and 3,600 W, 83% of it usable in The Solar Lab's test. Among 2 kWh units, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 measured 94%, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max 79%.

page.after:
What the differences mean

Why $1,000 is the line: on the makers' US stores read on 2026-11-26 and 27, the 2 kWh class (1,920 to 2,074 Wh) costs $649 to $999, and the first 3 kWh unit, the Pecron F3000LFP, is $899. Every row is $1,000 or less on its maker's store on the date read; for our rows that is the price through our link. Just over the line and left out: the 3,014.4 Wh BLUETTI Elite 300 at {after:bluetti-elite-300}.

The pick, the Pecron F3000LFP, is not a product Dealectric links, and we earn nothing from it. Dealectric does not test units: the efficiency and idle figures are The Solar Lab's, the specs are the makers', and the arithmetic below is ours.

  • Usable watt-hours = rated Wh × measured efficiency. Pecron: 3,072 × 0.83 = 2,550 Wh. Elite 200 V2: 2,073.6 × 0.94 = 1,949 Wh. Jackery: 2,042 × 0.90 = 1,838 Wh. S2000: 2,010 × 0.91 = 1,829 Wh. DELTA 3 Max: 2,048 × 0.79 = 1,618 Wh.
  • Cost per usable Wh = price ÷ usable Wh. Pecron: $899 ÷ 2,550 = 35.3¢. S2000: {after:anker-solix-s2000} ÷ 1,829 = 35.5¢. Elite 200 V2: {after:bluetti-elite-200-v2} ÷ 1,949 = 43.8¢. DELTA 3 Max: $879 ÷ 1,618 = 54.3¢. Jackery: $999 ÷ 1,838 = 54.4¢.
  • The rated order flips. Per rated Wh the DELTA 3 Max looks cheaper than the Elite 200 V2 at store prices: $879 ÷ 2,048 = 42.9¢ against {price:bluetti-elite-200-v2} ÷ 2,073.6 = 43.4¢. Per usable Wh it is 54.3¢ against {price:bluetti-elite-200-v2} ÷ 1,949 = 46.1¢.
  • Continuous watts per dollar. Pecron: 3,600 ÷ 899 = 4.00. Elite 200 V2: 2,600 W ÷ {after:bluetti-elite-200-v2} = 3.04. DELTA 3 Max: 2,400 ÷ 879 = 2.73. S2000: 1,500 W ÷ {after:anker-solix-s2000} = 2.31. Jackery: 2,200 ÷ 999 = 2.20.
  • Idle loss per day = idle watts × 24 h, with the unit left on and nothing plugged in. The Solar Lab says the AC inverter was on for the Pecron, DELTA 3 Max and S2000 figures; its Elite 200 V2 and Jackery reviews do not say. Pecron: 37 × 24 = 888 Wh (29% of its battery). DELTA 3 Max: 27 × 24 = 648 Wh (32%). Jackery: 17 × 24 = 408 Wh (20%). Elite 200 V2: 9.5 × 24 = 228 Wh (11%). S2000: 6 × 24 = 144 Wh (7%).
  • Estimated hours at a steady 100 W = usable Wh ÷ (100 W + idle W). Pecron: 2,550 ÷ 137 = 18.6 h. Elite 200 V2: 1,949 ÷ 109.5 = 17.8 h. S2000: 1,829 ÷ 106 = 17.3 h. Jackery: 1,838 ÷ 117 = 15.7 h. DELTA 3 Max: 1,618 ÷ 127 = 12.7 h. This is our estimate, not a test: it adds the reviewer's idle draw on top of the load. On the same sum the Elite 200 V2 outlasts the Pecron below an average load of about 80 W (both give about 21.8 h at 80 W).
UseFitsWhy
Most energy and outlet watts for the money, loads up to 3,600 WPecron F3000LFP35.3¢ per usable Wh and 4.00 W per dollar; ships mid-December. It weighs 63 lb and its surge is only 1.25 times its rating (4,500 ÷ 3,600).
Fridge, router and lights with the AC left on all dayBLUETTI Elite 200 V2 {buy:bluetti-elite-200-v2}Lowest losses of the 2,000 W-plus rows: 94% and 9.5 W. BLUETTI's page says orders placed on or after Nov. 18 ship in early January, which is why it is not the pick.
Light loads, long standby, easiest to carryAnker SOLIX S2000 {buy:anker-solix-s2000}About 6 W idle and 35.7 lb, but a 1,500 W outlet limit and a 7-13 week wait on orders from Nov 26.
Needed in the next two weeksEcoFlow DELTA 3 Max or Jackery Explorer 2000 v2EcoFlow's store lists the DELTA 3 Max as available; Jackery ships by Dec 11 and is the lightest 2,000 W-plus row at 39.5 lb. Both cost about 54¢ per usable Wh.

One spec to read carefully: BLUETTI's 3,900 W figure for the Elite 200 V2 is its Power Lifting mode, which BLUETTI's page limits to pure resistive loads such as kettles, electric blankets and hair dryers. It is not a motor-start surge rating, so it should not be set against EcoFlow's 4,800 W or Jackery's 4,400 W surge. The Solar Lab did hold a 3,000 W load on the Elite 200 V2 for over 2 minutes.

Measured efficiency and idle draw, collected

A power station never delivers its full rated watt-hours through the AC outlets: the inverter loses some in conversion, and it draws power for as long as it is switched on, even with nothing plugged in. The Solar Lab publishes both figures for each unit, which is why this page uses one reviewer throughout. Limits: its reviews carry no author or date, it states the test load only for the Pecron (3,600 W, full to empty), and it calls the Pecron and DELTA 3 Max idle figures calculated. As a cross-check, Dylan Dougherty at StorageReview drew 1.91 kWh from the Elite 200 V2, which is 1.91 ÷ 2.0736 = 92% of rated.

Two more units are measured or priced but are not in the table:

  • DJI Power 2000 (2,048 Wh, 3,000 W inverter, 48.5 lb per The Solar Lab): 84% and about 17 W idle, so 2,048 × 0.84 = 1,720 Wh usable. DJI's US store showed us a sign-in page in place of a price on 2026-11-27, so it has no row. The Gadgeteer listed it at $749.99 on Amazon on 2026-11-12; at that price it would cost $749.99 ÷ 1,720 = 43.6¢ per usable Wh, level with the Elite 200 V2 through our link.
  • ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 (1,920 Wh LiFePO4, 2,500 W, dispatch from Dec 4): {after:allpowers-r2500-v2-1920wh} through our link, or {after:allpowers-r2500-v2-1920wh} ÷ 1,920 = 30.4¢ per rated Wh, second only to the Pecron's $899 ÷ 3,072 = 29.3¢. It has no Solar Lab figures, so it has no row. Riccardo Conti (yourlifeupdated.net, 2026-08-07, tested in Italy) got 1.55 kWh out at a constant 100 W and 1.92 kWh at about 900 W, which is 81% and 100% of rated; idle draw was not part of that test. {buy:allpowers-r2500-v2-1920wh}

The Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO (2,048 Wh LiFePO4, 2,400 W, with a TT-30 RV outlet) is also under the line at {after:growatt-infinity-2000-pro} and also has no Solar Lab figures. {buy:growatt-infinity-2000-pro}

Not recommended

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max as a leave-it-on outage backup. It is the cheapest of the three big-brand 2,400 W-class rows per rated Wh, but it measured 79% and about 27 W idle, the weakest pair in the table: 331 Wh less per charge than the Elite 200 V2 (1,949 − 1,618) and 420 Wh more lost per idle day (648 − 228). Its $879 is the member price on EcoFlow's Black Friday page, dated Nov 26 to 30, with $1,199 shown for non-members, so it is under $1,000 only on sale. It does fit a buyer who needs a unit now and wants a published 4,800 W surge figure at 44.8 lb.

Sale dates: BLUETTI's and EcoFlow's Black Friday prices end Nov 30, 2026, and Anker's Black Friday sale for the S2000 is dated Nov 27 to 30. Jackery's $999 is a sale price against a $1,899 list price on its store, so that row is also under the line only on sale.
